title: GPU CI Warmup and Constraint-Aware Scheduler Runbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:
This runbook documents the recommended pattern and operational playbook for reducing GPU cold-starts and network-related delays for CI/eval workloads. It ties together three subsystems: the constraint-aware scheduler (k8s-gpu-scheduler), the warm-pool controller (gpu-warmpool-controller), and our Terraform landing-zone and network egress policy (iac-gpu-landing-zone). The goal is to reduce median CI job end-to-end latency by prewarming GPUs and minimizing image and model-fetch time, while preserving tenant isolation and egress SLOs.

Scope:
- CI/eval workloads that run transient jobs on shared GPU clusters (preflight tests, nightly evals, feature branches).
- Applies to cloud accounts using the centralized GPU landing-zone modules and the shared warm-pool.
- Not intended for Dedicated customer clusters (those have separate warm-pool rules).

Why this exists:
- We observed 40–60% of CI latency for GPU jobs caused by: image pull stalls, model artifact pulls from S3/private registries, and GPU kernel initialization that occurs on first allocation.
- Uncoordinated autoscaling can cause many pods to land on newly provisioned nodes, causing peak egress and image-pull congestion. This runbook defines controls to stagger warmups and bind affinity to cached nodes.

Ownership and cross-team responsibilities:
- eng-infra (primary): implement and operate k8s-gpu-scheduler and warm-pool controller, maintain Terraform modules.
- eng-ci (secondary): annotate CI jobs with scheduling hints and validate job-level timeouts.
- platform-security: review egress rules and approve IAM roles for prefetch agents.

SLOs and observable thresholds:
- Median CI GPU job runtime (queue->completion): target < 9m for preflight jobs (current baseline 12m).
- Cold-start tail 95th percentile (first token latency for models): < 60s.
- Image pull error rate during scale-up: < 0.5%.
- Egress sustained throughput for warm-pool seeding: < 500 MB/s per region to avoid billing spikes.

Key signals / dashboards to monitor:
- metric: gpu.warmpool.available_size (gauge)
- metric: gpu.scheduler.queue_length_by_priority (timeseries)
- metric: container.image_pull_duration (p50/p95)
- metric: network.egress_bytes_per_minute (per-account)
- alert: GPU_WARMPOOL_UNDERPROVISIONED (available_size < configured_min for 10m)
- alert: IMAGE_PULL_ERR_RATE_HIGH (region > 0.5% for 5m)

Configuration matrix (recommended defaults):
| Setting | Default | Rationale |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| warmpool.min_size | 6 | Enough to run parallel preflight jobs during burst windows |
| warmpool.preseed_images | [redwood/llm-runtime:prod, private-registry/model-cache:latest] | images to pre-pull |
| scheduler.constraint_window_seconds | 120 | stagger scheduling decisions to avoid thundering herd |
| egress.rate_limit_mb_per_region | 500 | soft cap on seeding throughput to protect billing |
| terraform.module_version | v2025-11-ops | pinned stable IaC module for warmpool + network |

Implementation snippets and examples:
1) CI job annotations (to be added to job definitions in the CI pipeline YAML):
```
annotations:
  redwood.com/gpu-warmup: "required"
  redwood.com/scheduling-hint: "cache_affinity:high,priority:preflight"
  redwood.com/egress-budget-mb: "50"
```

2) Kubernetes pod affinity snippet used by the scheduler to prefer nodes with seeded images:
```
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      preference:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: node.kubernetes.io/gpu-cache-populated
          operator: In
          values:
          - "true"
```

3) Terraform variables (example) for the iac-gpu-landing-zone module:
```
module "gpu_lz" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/infra/iac-gpu-landing-zone.git?ref=v2025-11-ops"

  warmpool_min_size = 6
  warmpool_regions = ["us-west-2", "eu-west-1"]
  preseed_registry = "private-registry.internal:443"
  egress_throttle_mb = 500
}
```

Operational run steps (fast path for platform engineers):
1) Incident: CI GPU jobs queue grows > 30 and warmpool.available_size == 0.
  - Owner: eng-infra oncall.
  - Immediate action: run `kubectl get pods -n gpu-warmpool-controller` and check errors.
2) Validate egress throttling: check network.egress_bytes_per_minute for the account.
  - If above egress.rate_limit_mb_per_region, temporarily increase `egress_throttle_mb` in the Terraform staging workspace (not production) and reapply to allow catch-up seeding.
3) Force preseed run: trigger the warmpool preseed job with higher concurrency: `kubectl -n infra run -i --rm preseed-trigger --image=infra/preseed:latest -- /bin/sh -c 'preseed --concurrency 8'`
4) If image-pull errors persist: inspect registry auth and IAM role used by warmpool-controller (`role/warmpool-prefetcher`). Rotate short-lived token if needed.
5) Rollback: if changes to IaC are causing instability, revert commit in terraform-staging and promote last stable tag `v2025-11-ops` using the CI release pipeline.

Postmortem checklist (when incidents occur):
- Collect: scheduler logs (k8s-gpu-scheduler), warmpool-controller logs, image-pull errors, node startup metrics.
- Compute: % of jobs impacted by cold-start vs network stalls.
- Update: warmpool.min_size or preseed_images based on the breakdown.
- Retro: schedule a game-day to exercise runbook.

Safety and access controls:
- Warm-pool controllers run in a dedicated namespace `infra-gpu-warmpool` and assume `role/warmpool-prefetcher`. Only eng-infra IAM principals may alter role bindings.
- Terraform changes to the landing-zone module require a two-person approval and a successful canary apply in `terraform-ci` workspace.

Maintenance tasks (weekly/monthly):
- Weekly: rotate prefetch credentials, validate preseed image list and size.
- Monthly: run a simulated scale test (canary) that increases warmpool.preseed concurrency to validate egress caps and image registry behavior.
- Quarterly: review scheduler.constraint_window_seconds and adjust based on observed queueing patterns.

Troubleshooting tips and common failures:
- Symptom: jobs stuck in ImagePullBackOff during scale-up.
  - Likely causes: registry rate limit, IAM quota, node-level docker config mismatches. Check cloud provider registry quota and containerd logs.
- Symptom: sudden spike in network.egress_bytes_per_minute after deploy.
  - Likely causes: changed preseed image list or image digest rotation. Reconcile preseed_images list and pin digests in Terraform module.
- Symptom: cold-start 95th increases despite warmpool available.
  - Likely causes: KV cache miss for model shard (model-cache not seeded). Add model artifact IDs to warmpool preseed list and verify S3 presigned URL latencies.

Rollout and testing guidance for changes to scheduler/warmpool code:
1) Feature branch: add unit tests for scheduling heuristics and a feature flag defaulted off.
2) Canary: deploy to staging `gpu-warmpool-controller` with warmpool.min_size = 2 and run 20 synthetic preflight jobs. Verify image pull p95 < 20s.
3) Gradual rollout: promote to us-west-2 with warmpool.min_size = 4, monitor metrics for 48h.
4) Full rollout: bump Terraform module version and follow the two-person approval flow.

Appendix A — Example emergency commands:
- Check warmpool status: `kubectl -n infra get warmpools`
- Trigger manual preseed: `kubectl -n infra exec -it deploy/gpu-warmpool-controller -- preseed --images-from tfvars`
- Inspect scheduler metrics: `kubectl -n infra port-forward svc/gpu-scheduler-metrics 9000:9000` then curl http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep gpu.scheduler
